title: Streamlined VPC telemetry Terraform module (prometheus, grafana, otel, log-shipping)
creator: Marisa Kline
description: Create a reusable, parameterized Terraform module for VPC-hosted observability stacks that installs Prometheus (operator or helm), Grafana (helm), an OpenTelemetry Collector deployment (or DaemonSet as option), and a log-shipping agent (Vector) with opinionated defaults and production-ready health checks. The goal is to replace ad-hoc per-customer manifests and reduce upgrade friction across on-prem/VPC installs.
upgrade_strategy: Module releases will follow semver. Each release will include an upgrade guide with tfstate migration steps for renamed resources. We will support a canary upgrade pattern: deploy new module into a canary cell (configurable count) with traffic routed via smart routing flags. Provide automated plan-only CI job to surface diffs and a staged apply workflow that requires manual approval for production namespaces.
health_checks: Otel Collector readiness + liveliness probes (endpoints /healthz and /metrics)
Prometheus scrape targets check: ensure >=90% of expected targets are UP after apply
Prometheus rule for Alertmanager connectivity and rule evaluation latency
Grafana API health: login + API query test for pinned dashboards
Vector log-forwarder delivery success rate metric (backpressure/hwm alerts)
End-to-end synthetic pipeline check: generate test log/event, assert arrival in destination (s3/es) within 30s
rollout_plan: 1) Create feature branch and initial module with helm providers and basic values
2) Smoke deploy into dev cell (dev-vpc) with minimal resources
3) Run automated integration tests (see testing_plan) and iterate
4) Deploy to staging cell, enable canary mode (1-2 nodes) and measure health checks for 24h
5) Run data-plane failover tests (simulate OTEL load and log sink downtime)
6) Gradual rollout to production cells with manual approval gates and post-apply verification script
7) Publish upgrade notes and module registry entry after successful production rollout
testing_plan: Unit: terraform validate + tflint + module unit tests with terratest
Integration: deploy into ephemeral k8s clusters in CI and assert health checks and metrics
Chaos: simulate node restarts and network partition to validate collector resilience
Performance: run synthetic scrape load for Prometheus and verify scrape latency and memory usage
E2E: create synthetic log, verify ingestion into configured sink (S3/ELK) and dashboard visibility
risks: Upgrading helm chart versions may change CRD schemas for prometheus-operator leading to tfstate drift
Collector configuration mistakes can cause silent drop of spans/logs if buffer sizes are misconfigured
Large tenants could need custom resource sizing; opinionated defaults may not fit every customer
Terraform provider mismatches across teams (helm/versioned providers) could cause apply failures
decisions: Use Helm provider + wrapper module instead of raw manifests to simplify upgrades and values overrides
Expose resource sizing and persistence flags as top-level module inputs (not buried in values)
Default log sink is configurable; include S3 + Elastic as supported destinations via provider plugins
Include optional managed Grafana provisioning for enterprise customers, otherwise deploy OSS Grafana
acceptance_criteria: Module published to internal terraform registry with semantic versions
Automated CI runs validate module for terraform 1.4+ and provider matrix
Health checks pass in dev and staging cells for 48h under synthetic load
Upgrade path documented and tested (import steps + example upgrade plan)
At least one private deployment migrated to new module in canary mode without data loss
